# Citation

Shi, J., Tian, Z., Lai, J., and Huang, X. (2023). Plant pan-genomics and its applications. *Molecular Plant* 16, 168–186. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.molp.2022.12.009 (PDF p. 1).

# One-Sentence Summary

This review explains how plant pan-genomes capture core and variable DNA, how structural variation and genome-assembly methods shape them, and how pan-genomes can improve genetic studies and breeding (PDF pp. 1–19).

# Research Question

What drives variable plant genome sequences, how can plant pan-genomes be represented and completed, and what applications do they enable in genetics and breeding? This paraphrases the review scope (PDF pp. 1–3).

# Biological System

The subject is plant species and their intra-specific genome diversity, with examples from Arabidopsis, rice, maize, soybean, wheat, barley, tomato, potato, cotton and other crops (PDF pp. 1–6, Table 1).

# Study Design

Narrative review of plant pan-genome construction, structural variation, assembly representation, gapless or telomere-to-telomere genomes and genetic/breeding applications (PDF pp. 1–19, Figures 1–3). A new comparative pan-genome analysis by the authors: Not reported.

# Data

The review synthesizes published assemblies, resequencing studies, structural-variation analyses and pan-genome resources. It reports examples of population sizes and pan-genome representations in Table 1, but provides no unified raw data matrix (PDF pp. 5–10, Table 1).

# Methods

- Describe structural-variation sources including transposable elements, non-allelic homologous recombination, introgression or horizontal gene transfer and fractionation after polyploidization (PDF pp. 3–5, Figure 1).
- Review short-read structural-variant detection, map-to-pan construction, high-quality assembly comparison and graph-based pan-genomes (PDF pp. 5–10, Figure 2).
- Summarize gapless or telomere-to-telomere plant genome progress (PDF pp. 10–15, Table 2).
- Discuss applications to genetic mapping, missing heritability, epigenomic mapping, genome editing and de novo domestication (PDF pp. 15–18, Figure 3).

# Software and Versions

The review discusses computational strategies and tools in the cited literature but does not specify one software environment or version set used by the authors. Exact software versions: Not reported (PDF pp. 5–10).

# Important Parameters

Important considerations include genome assembly quality, read length, structural-variant size and complexity, representation method, reference bias, population size and the degree of sequence diversity captured (PDF pp. 3–10). Universal numerical thresholds: Not reported.

# Inputs and Outputs

Inputs include genome assemblies, short- and long-read sequence data, population resequencing data and annotation resources. Outputs include core and variable genome sequences, structural-variant calls, graph or linear pan-genome representations and candidate loci for genetics or breeding (PDF pp. 1–10, 15–18).

# Main Results

The review defines a plant pan-genome as the collection of core and variable DNA sequences in a species and emphasizes that plant genomes contain substantial sequence diversity (PDF pp. 1–3). It identifies transposable elements, non-allelic homologous recombination, introgression or horizontal transfer and fractionation as major drivers of variable sequences (PDF pp. 3–5, Figure 1). The authors argue that graph and high-quality pan-genome references can reduce reference bias, reveal additional loci and support breeding applications (PDF pp. 10–18, Figure 3).

# Assumptions

Pan-genome applications assume that additional assemblies and structural variants capture biologically meaningful diversity and that improved references reduce biases present in a single linear reference (PDF pp. 1–3, 15–18).

# Limitations

The review notes that complex structural variants are difficult to detect and represent, non-genic regions remain incomplete in draft assemblies, and graph or pan-genome analysis requires substantial sequencing and computational resources (PDF pp. 5–12).

# Reproducible Implementation Details

No single accession set, assembly pipeline, structural-variant caller, graph-construction command, filtering threshold or software lockfile is reported. Exact implementation details: Not reported (PDF pp. 5–12).

# Relevance to simitall

**Inference, not an author recommendation:** Pan-genome concepts could inform simitall support for structural-variant-aware references, reference-bias documentation and genotype-to-trait evidence. The paper does not mention or evaluate simitall (PDF pp. 1–19).

# Terminology

- **Pan-genome:** Collection of all non-redundant DNA sequences in a species, including core and variable regions (PDF pp. 1–3).
- **Core genome:** Sequences shared broadly among individuals of a species (PDF pp. 1–3).
- **Variable or dispensable genome:** Sequences present in only a subset of individuals (PDF pp. 1–3).
- **Graph pan-genome:** Genome representation that uses alternative paths to represent sequence diversity (PDF pp. 5–10, Figure 2).
